correctness.rationale: Idempotent P is Lie-Nijenhuis exactly if image and kernel are complementary Lie subalgebras: torsion on U×U and K×K gives their closure, and mixed torsion cancels automatically. Every subalgebra in codimension-one extension L=Ft⊕V lies in V or is W+F(t+u) with A-invariant W. The exhaustive three cases (only U outside V, only K outside V, both outside V) yield respectively q^[r(m-r+1)] I_{m-r}, q^[r(m-r+1)] I_{r-1}, and (q-1)q^m D_{r-1,m-r}. In the both-outside case W+K is a hyperplane and exactly (q-1)/q of coset differences avoid it. This proves symmetry under I-P, boundary counts N0=N_{m+1}=1, the single Jordan block/irreducible extremes and squarefree factorization. Own GF(2),m=2 direct testing of the ORIGINAL torsion and idempotence identities over all 512 linear endomorphisms gave scalar A ranks (1,28,28,1) and irreducible A ranks (1,4,4,1), matching the formula.
residual_risks: Prime-field small enumeration corroborates but does not prove formula for arbitrary m, q and all rational-canonical actions; the proof uses general subspace/coset structure.

value.rationale: The full rank distribution is an exact natural invariant of Nijenhuis projections on a canonical solvable Lie-algebra family. Its three structural pieces and parameter A-dependence differentiate single Jordan blocks, scalar actions, irreducible actions and squarefree modules, detecting rank gaps that subalgebra classification alone does not supply. A researcher studying Nijenhuis splittings could use those exact labeled distributions.
residual_risks: Does not give an efficient closed enumeration of disjoint invariant pairs for arbitrary wild module types; this limitation is explicit and does not negate the structural formula.
